market_context.summary: Malaysian e-commerce is concentrated on app-first platforms: Google, Temasek and Bain put 2026 e-commerce GMV at USD 25 billion (+22%), while the official DOSM e-commerce income series, which also counts business-to-business sales, reached RM937.5 billion in the first nine months of 2025. Ipsos's May 2026 survey found 71% of online purchasers had bought on Shopee and 62% on TikTok in the past six months, with Lazada down to 5%; Euromonitor says Shopee and TikTok Shop recorded almost equivalent sales in 2025. Beauty is moving online quickly: 45% of online purchasers bought beauty care products or cosmetics (29% a year earlier) and 28% personal care products. Health and beauty chains (Watsons, Guardian) and pharmacies (CARiNG, BIG) sell online in their own right, but brand owners' own sites mostly route shoppers to official stores on Shopee and Lazada. No regulator-verified platform market shares were found.

key_facts.fact: Among Malaysians who bought online in the past six months (N=621, May 2026): Shopee 71%, TikTok 62%, Facebook 12%, Lazada 5% (2025: 74%, 52%, 1%, 11%).

key_facts.fact: 60% of Malaysians aged 18-74 bought on an e-commerce platform in the past six months; among purchasers, 45% bought beauty care products or cosmetics (29% in 2025), 28% personal care products (20%) and 25% healthcare products (15%).

ranking_method_note: Scores (1-5) were assigned by the researcher from evidence retrieved on 2026-11-26 and applied to the fixed rubric: weighted_score = 0.20*ecommerce_significance + 0.25*beauty_category_relevance + 0.20*consumer_reach + 0.15*brand_competitor_coverage + 0.20*data_integration_feasibility, rounded to 2 decimals; priority_rank = rank by weighted_score within the country; ties broken by beauty_category_relevance, then consumer_reach as specified. Where a tie survived both rubric tie-breaks, three further deterministic tie-breaks were added by the researcher (not part of the brief): higher ecommerce_significance, then the higher in-country monthly web-visit estimate (Semrush, October 2026, as cited in each record), then alphabetical order. Scoring anchors used consistently across the three countries: consumer_reach 5 = >=10M estimated in-country monthly web visits or an equivalent survey-evidenced scale, 4 = 2-10M (or >=1M company-reported active app users), 3 = 0.5-2M, 2 = 100-500K, 1 = <100K or no credible number; brand_competitor_coverage 5 = >=8 of the 12 reference mass-market brands verified as listed, 4 = 5-7 verified or brand-owner official stores verified, 3 = 2-4 verified or a full-range retailer whose assortment could not be verified (neutral), 2 = mass brands largely absent / unverified limited-range or unbranded platform, 1 = verified absent; data_integration_feasibility 5 = documented official API exposing catalogue and competitive price/offer data, 4 = open developer portal with a documented seller API on a platform where brand owners run their own stores (own-shop data only) or public storefront data readable without login, 3 = public pages retrievable without an API, or a seller API whose reference was not verified or that only helps a brand that sells on that platform, 2 = automated access refused or app/location-gated with no usable API, 1 = app-only. The beauty_relevance and data_collection_feasibility labels follow the scores (4-5 high, 3 medium, 1-2 low). Web-visit estimates understate app-first platforms; no regulator-verified or audited market-share figure was found for any platform, so every reach figure is a third-party estimate, a survey result or company-reported. Scores are judgements, not measurements. In this file one tie survived both rubric tie-breaks: GrabMart and foodpanda (both 2.65, beauty relevance 3, reach 3, significance 3); GrabMart is ranked higher on the Semrush estimate of Malaysian visits (grab.com 2.87M across all Grab services against foodpanda.my 1.74M), which is a weak basis. Temu ranks above ZALORA (both 2.40) through the rubric's own reach tie-break.

data_integration_feasibility.note: Documented Open Platform API for own-shop data; public pages are gated.

platforms.priority_rationale: The default destination for online shopping in Malaysia and the place where mass-market brand owners themselves run flagship stores; highest reach, strong category evidence and a documented API.
platforms.confidence_note: A nationally representative survey, two traffic estimators and several brand-owner sites agree; sales share is not verified and traffic estimates are volatile.
